Mechanism family: quasi-random-discrepancy-restarts
Replacement scope: Replace the SA seeding and move-proposal randomness (numpy default_rng) with low-discrepancy Halton-sequence-driven restarts and proposals inside the existing SA loop; keep the SA structure, objective, and incumbent fallback unchanged.
Gain mechanism: Pseudo-random restarts cluster and leave systematic holes in the assignment lattice; a Halton quasi-random sequence gives provably more uniform coverage of the discrete assignment space per iteration, so the same 20,000-iteration budget explores strictly more distinct basins and finds lower maxima on multimodal instances.
Compute budget: Same iteration count as incumbent (20,000 per seed, ≤ 2 seeds); Halton generation is O(1) per draw, so evaluation time is unchanged or slightly lower.
Plan: (1) Implement a small Halton generator: for dimension d use base = (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ...), radical-inverse function, with a fixed skip of 100 to avoid initial correlation. (2) Draw restarts: for each of R = 8 restarts, generate an initial assignment by mapping Halton draws to GPU indices with memory-feasibility repair (if a GPU overflows, reassign the model to the Halton-next GPU with room). (3) Use Halton draws for move selection too: index i = floor(h1·n), target g = floor(h2·gpu_num), swap-vs-move flag from h3 < 0.5.
